correctness.rationale: From the exact gamma shape–rate mixture, its Laplace transform and PGF follow algebraically. The continuous Lévy density is positive; its kernel decreases exactly when the derivative at zero is nonpositive. All compound-Poisson coefficients are positive because \(0\le a\le q<1\). The candidate Bernoulli-thinning innovation has exact degree-\(n\) log coefficient \(\nu_n(c)=[b_n(1)-b_n(c)]/n\). The derivative identity and global bound show its nonnegativity at every degree and retention exactly when \((r+1)(\theta+s)^2\ge s(\theta+1)^2\). Outside this region, the degree-one coefficient is negative for retentions close to one, proving necessity. The factorial-Palm formula follows by differentiation at every nonnegative integer order. Exact rational checks passed after executing the embedded script; finite checks do not substitute for the all-index proof.

value.rationale: The originating PNXL model is motivated by count-data autoregressions, where stationary-marginal Bernoulli-thinning closure is a materially different question from merely using a distribution as innovations. The exact global rate threshold provides a complete model feasibility boundary and explicit innovations; the structural separation shows Poissonization can restore discrete self-decomposability despite non-self-decomposable continuous mixing. The all-order factorial-Palm critical family follows naturally from size-biased/event-sampled counts rather than an arbitrary small parameter slice. A concrete rational witness shows actual nontrivial contrast. The work claims neither a general mixed-Poisson theorem nor an independent audit.
